**Notes**

* Add some notes here
* Use markdown
SET key value [EX seconds | PX milliseconds] [NX | XX]

key — the name you're storing the value under

value — the string to store

EX seconds — optional expiry in seconds or PX milliseconds — optional expiry in milliseconds

NX — optional, only set if the key does not already exist or XX — optional, only set if the key already exists
→ stores the value "sayantan" under key session:abc123, and it auto-expires after 3600 seconds (1 hour).

key — the name of the key you want the value of
No value, no optional flags — it's a pure read.
→ returns the value stored at that key, or nil if the key doesn't exist or has expired.

The official documentation for the GETEX command contains the following:

GETEX key [EX seconds|PX milliseconds|EXAT unix-time-seconds|PXAT unix-time-milliseconds|PERSIST]
With that in mind, is the following command valid?

GETEX key EX 5 PX 1000
(Hint: try to run this command in RBook)

No, that command is **not valid**.

**Why:** In the syntax `[EX seconds|PX milliseconds|EXAT unix-time-seconds|PXAT unix-time-milliseconds|PERSIST]`, the `|` means "or" — these options are mutually exclusive alternatives, not combinable flags. The `[ ]` around the whole group means the entire expiry option is optional, but if you choose one, you can only choose **one**.

`GETEX key EX 5 PX 1000` tries to pass both `EX 5` and `PX 1000` at the same time, which violates that "pick one" rule. Redis will reject it with an error like:
```
(error) ERR syntax error
```

**Valid examples instead:**
```
GETEX key EX 5              -- expire in 5 seconds
GETEX key PX 1000           -- expire in 1000 milliseconds
GETEX key PERSIST           -- remove any existing expiry
GETEX key                   -- just fetch the value, no expiry change (fully optional)
```
Any one of these is fine — just never two expiry-style options together in the same call.
